NOTE: Apologies in advance for some of the photos not being all that great. There was a lot of drinking and back in 2009 I had the crappiest quality digital camera possible.

In 2009, myself and one of my best friends decided to say 'fuck it' and took a red-eye flight out to Las Vegas for a four day weekend. It was one of best trips of my life.

We arrived in Vegas around 3am local time and checked into our hotel, the [lovely MGM Grand](http://i.imgur.com/Nj47Y8u.jpg). We were able to get a good deal as it was during the recession, and Vegas was trying to bring in tourists. It was something like $400 total for the flight, hotel and included a free show.

After dumping our bags in our rooms, we took off, for [Vegas is most alive at night](http://i.imgur.com/unDtfRa.jpg).

Drinks in hand (you can drink on the street in Vegas, if you didn't know), we walked up and down the strip, people watching, looking out for the Elvis impersonators we'd heard so much about. The people were friendly - but then again, how could you not be? Vegas is like adult Disney, after all.

We returned to our rooms around 6 and slept.

The next day started with[ shots](http://i.imgur.com/WbguOvM.jpg), which are bigger than the shots in Jersey. We wandered. Explored casinos. Neither of us gamble, but we toured the place. At some point we had 20$ all you can eat sushi.

Drunk and happy, we contemplated finding a chapel and seeing if they would perform a fake same-sex marriage just for the hell of it, but the cheapest wedding we could find was $700 and since we weren't in love and just wanted a funny story, we decided not to do it. Our money would be put to better use later, anyway.

We only had 4 days, and we hadn't rented a car, so we didn't get to see some of the cooler stuff like the [neon sign graveyard](http://www.neonmuseum.org/), but we did make a trip to the edge of the strip. There, we found one of the most terrifying places I've ever been to.

If you're ever in Vegas and want to give yourself nightmares, take a stop at [Circus Circus](http://i.imgur.com/csn6AHU.jpg). The place is circus themed and goddamn terrifying. Clowns, everywhere. The best way I can describe it is as an overgrown version of Chucky Cheese, but scarier. I didn't take any photos, but I'll never forget the frightening blur of the place.

Thankfully, our next stop made up for it. The Hilton was holding the annual Star Trek convention. The hotel was made to look like [the control room](http://i.imgur.com/8Ap48kW.jpg) of [the Enterprise](http://i.imgur.com/JGjQZXE.jpg).

I am not a big Star Trek fan, but my friend is. She's been madly in love with Captain Kirk since she was a kid, so of course, we had to go.

[She met some Klingons](http://i.imgur.com/TmL2nr6.jpg). She met some guy who had a bunch of poodles that he dressed in Star Fleet uniforms. We met a bunch of other Star Trek fans. The line to meet Shatner was long, so she didn't go. She met him later in NYC, though.

Of course, no trip to Vegas is complete without a Vegas [tattoo](http://i.imgur.com/aIHKEMM.jpg). We got semi-matching ones. Both had dice, mine was a Sailor Jerry custom design. Hers was dice made of skulls.

There was more drinking, hence the potato/crappy quality of some of these photos. But I'd still advise anyone looking for a good time to head on over to the Nevada desert and check in to one of the better hotels. Why? [Because.](http://i.imgur.com/HDGXFAK.jpg)

Canton teen uses invention to spread kind words (article in comments to avoid ad)

CANTON — Some days, all a person needs is a positive word or a motivational phrase to pull them out of a gloomy mood. Jake C. Russell, 13, has come up with a way to provide those words of encouragement to the community.

Jake’s new invention, Posi-bot, has been set up at Canton Free Library for anyone who’d like to pick up a pocket-sized note to brighten his or her day.

“I know sometimes people have a bad day and they could use something to lift their day or to make their spirits feel good,” Jake said.

The Canton teen came up with the idea in September when he was making cardboard robots with a classmate at the Deep Root Center, where he attends school.

Deep Root Center for Self-Directed Learning is a community resource learning center that provides each member a unique educational program, based on their personal interests and passions, through classes, Pathways, one-on-one tutorials, as well as materials, tools and resources for independent projects and research, according to the learning center’s blog.

Deep Root Center’s executive director and founder, Maria L. Corse, said she was very proud of Jake for coming up with the idea and was happy to see him see the project through. She said the idea was characteristic of Jake.

“He’s a really empathetic kid,” Mrs. Corse said. “This is totally true-to-nature for him.” Jake’s invention doesn’t only pass out positive notes, however. If you feel so inclined, you may write your own helpful words and slip them into Posi-bot for others to enjoy.

“I think maybe if people can be generous maybe it will make their day even better,” Jake said. “They feel good because they are making someone else’s day, so they’re going to feel even more great.”

Jake spent months piecing Posi-bot together, which is made from an old computer, a few pieces of wood and some soup and coffee cans. The inspiration for the giving and taking of messages was inspired by the little library boxes that have been placed in several locations around the village by the Canton Free Library and Canton Rotary.

Canton Free Library Director Emily M. Owen was excited when she was approached by Jake about the project. Deep Root students are frequent patrons of the library and Ms. Owen was happy to house Posi-bot. “We thought it was a great fit for the library,” Ms. Owen said. “I hope it will brighten people’s day.”

I found a couple of inspiring titles on stratcom reading list of all places, is in itself an intriguing development.

Turn the Ship Around! – L. David Marquet - © 2013, Penguin Press

"Leadership should mean giving control rather than taking control and creating leaders rather than forging followers." Turn the Ship Around! Is the true story of how the Santa Fe skyrocketed from worst to first in the fleet by challenging the U.S. Navy's traditional leader-follower approach. Struggling against his own instincts to take control, he instead achieved the vastly more powerful model of giving control. Before long, each member of Marquet's crew became a leader and assumed responsibility for everything he did, from clerical tasks to crucial combat decisions. The crew became fully engaged, contributing their full intellectual capacity every day, and the Santa Fe started winning awards and promoting a highly disproportionate number of officers to submarine command. No matter your business or position, you can apply Marquet's radical guidelines to turn your own ship around. The payoff: a workplace where everyone around you is taking responsibility for their actions, where people are healthier and happier, where everyone is a leader.

Leaders Eat Last – Simon Sinek - © 2014, Penguin Press

Imagine a world where almost everyone wakes up inspired to go to work, feels trusted and valued during the day, then returns home feeling fulfilled. This is not a crazy, idealized notion. Today, in many successful organizations, great leaders are creating environments in which people naturally work together to do remarkable things. Today's workplaces tend to be full of cynicism, paranoia and self-interest. But the best organizations foster trust and cooperation because their leaders build what Sinek calls a Circle of Safety that separates the security inside the team from the challenges outside. The Circle of Safety leads to stable, adaptive, confident teams, where everyone feels they belong and all energies are devoted to facing the common enemy and seizing big opportunities. Sinek illustrates his ideas with fascinating true stories from a wide range of examples, from the military to manufacturing, from government to investment banking.
